ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A square single-turn coil abcd with a resistance of $0.1\Omega$ has a side length of $0.2\mathrm{m}$. The side bc coincides with the edge of a uniform magnetic field. The width of the magnetic field is equal to the side length of the coil, and the magnetic induction strength is $0.5\mathrm{T}$. Under the action of a horizontal pulling force, the coil moves to the right through the magnetic field region at a speed of $8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$.

1. What is the magnitude of the induced electromotive force $E$ in the coil during the above process?
2. What is the magnitude of the tension force $F$ experienced by the coil during the aforementioned process?
3. What is the heat $Q$ generated by the induced current in the coil during the aforementioned process?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a square single-turn coil abcd, and the right side bc of the coil is exactly against a vertical dashed boundary. Between the vertical dashed lines is a uniform magnetic field region; within the region, multiple “×” symbols indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward, labeled B. The horizontal width of the magnetic field region is the same as the side length of the coil. The dashed square frame on the right indicates a certain position after the coil moves to the right through the magnetic field, showing that the coil passes to the right through this magnetic field region under the action of a horizontal pulling force. Reasoning: The side length of the coil is l=0.2 m, the resistance is R=0.1 Ω, the magnetic induction intensity is B=0.5 T, and the speed is v=8 m/s. When the coil enters or leaves the magnetic field, the magnetic flux passing through the coil changes, and the rate of change of the overlapping area is dA/dt=lv, so the magnitude of the induced electromotive force is E=B(dA/dt)=Blv=0.5×0.2×8=0.8 V. The induced current is I=E/R=0.8/0.1=8 A. In order to make the coil move at a uniform speed, the magnitude of the external pulling force is equal to the magnitude of the resistance force of the magnetic field on the current-carrying side, F=BIl=0.5×8×0.2=0.8 N. Because the width of the magnetic field is equal to the side length of the coil, from the time the coil starts to enter until it completely leaves, there is an entering distance l and a leaving distance l, and the total time for which the induced current exists is t=2l/v=2×0.2/8=0.05 s. The Joule heat is Q=I^2Rt=8^2×0.1×0.05=0.32 J.
